messages:
ashley: deploy-bot flagged a stalled canary in eu-west — preflight hook job failing due to pod TTL annotation. rolling window starts in ~25m, auto-rollback will trigger if we don't act. @matt @sara any thoughts?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Release 2026.03.21-rc2 canary paused — preflight failed -> hook job 'db-seed' exited, ttl=60s. scheduled auto-rollback in 30m unless overridden. see /deploy/logs/2387654321

matt: looking now. if the hook job has ttl=60s it's likely getting killed before completion. options: bump TTL, add `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation`, or run the hook as a separate job outside the canary. mid-rollout chart changes are risky.

sara: agree — safest is to exempt this release from auto-rollback, pin the chart to the last known-good (3.5.1?) and do a staggered manual rollout (maxUnavailable=1) across the zone. keeps impact small and buys time for a proper chart patch.

ashley: +1. plan: 1) create deploy-bot override to disable auto-rollback for this thread 2) pin to chart 3.5.1 for remaining canary pods 3) run staggered upgrade with maxUnavailable=1. i'll create the override now.

olivia: I'll draft release notes and the rollback playbook. adding quick commands below for the runbook:

```
# pin back to last-good if we need to revert
helm upgrade myservice redwood/myservice --version 3.5.0 -f values-canary.yaml --namespace prod --timeout 10m
# or apply staggered rollout (k8s patch for deployment)
kubectl patch deployment myservice -n prod -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"rollingUpdate":{"maxUnavailable":1}}}}'
```

matt: patching chart pin & starting the stagger now. tagging @ci-bot to run preflight after pin.

ci-bot: ci-bot: preflight job queued -> job id 2387654350. logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/2387654350 :eyes:

ashley: thanks — if preflight passes we un-exempt and continue staggered rollout. if it fails, follow rollback playbook above and open an incident if >2 regions impacted. :thumbsup:
